Are You an Introvert Or Are You Maybe an Undercover Narcissist?

It makes some sense to me because I've known introverted people, but also people who seem introverted but oddly egotistical. People come in all shades of personalities I guess. I've always found it strange how we identify as introvert or extrovert. Seems oversimplified.
Since when did doing what you want to do and managing your own affairs become narcissistic? That doesn't even approach clinical narcissism.
Purely semantics. There was nothing scientific about any of that bullshit.

The writer is consulting and linking to white papers (one link is broken, the other 2 are open access) and an original blog from Scientific American, so I think he has a pretty good scientific basis in consideration of it being psychology.
Self reporting and psychology don't mix well, and lack of metrics for the "study" mean there's nothing there but fluff.

"Assessing Hypersensitive Narcissism: A Reexamination of Murray’s Narcism Scale" which is one of the cited papers uses and MMPI-based composite measure and has a sample size of over 400, so they are using current diagnostic standards, and that is a pretty good sample size.

The Wink, 1991 study is also available on open access. From what I've gathered, that was the ground-laying study for this hypothesis. His study looks at correlation issues between diagnostic evaluations for narcissism. His sample size was 350, which is a bit smaller. The p-value for his results is good (0.05/0.01), so his statistical analysis should be reliable.

Self-reporting is, I believe, a necessary evil of psychology. That's part of what sets it apart from other fields. It is just its nature. It can't really operate any other way without a mind reading machine. The follow up studies have supported the Wink 1991 paper pretty well though, so all that can truly be said is that there is a growing body of evidence to continue to build on, and perhaps the recognition of different manifestations of narcissism will lead to better diagnostic tools and better treatments.
And this is precisely why psychology gets such a bad rep. I mean, we're talking about an article that ends in an "are you a narcissist?" quiz.
